IMPORTANT LIMIT: it does NOT extend to ITAR-controlled content, and Canada was deliberately excluded from the AUKUS ITAR exemption at 22 CFR 126.7 - so Australia-UK enjoy a broader licence-free ITAR regime than Canada.

name: Arrangement between the New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment and the Australian Space Agency Regarding Space Cooperation for Peaceful Purposes
scope: Bilateral civil space arrangement for cooperation in the peaceful use of space. Expressly NON-BINDING. Establishes a Joint Steering Committee, and lists SPACE SITUATIONAL AWARENESS among its areas of cooperation, alongside a trans-Tasman space innovation ecosystem covering orbital and suborbital missions, ground segment networks and remote asset management.
notes: THE ONLY BILATERAL AUSTRALIA-NZ SPACE INSTRUMENT IDENTIFIED. Document personally retrieved and read in collection. SOURCING TRAP: the '2023-04' string in the space.gov.au PDF path is a CMS upload folder, NOT a date - the arrangement is dated 22 October 2019, and any record citing it as a 2023 instrument is wrong. Two features carry the analytical weight: it is non-binding (so it commits nothing), and its SSA clause plus the standing Joint Steering Committee give an existing, signed, governed venue into which SDA cooperation could be tabled without negotiating a new instrument. Confidence Medium pending a second read of the operative text.
label: FACT
source_title: The Australian Space Agency and New Zealand's Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment

name: Catalyst: Strategic - Australia New Zealand Collaborative Space Programme
scope: Bilateral space research programme: from January 2024 the NZ Space Agency partnered with Australia's SmartSat CRC (now the Australasian Space Innovation Institute, ASII). MBIE funded eight feasibility studies; three were scaled up, all running 1 March 2026 - February 2029, with NZ contributions of NZ$977,000 to NZ$2.84m. Funded through MBIE's Catalyst Fund, whose research priorities explicitly include 'Space and Earth observation'.
notes: The defence-relevant project is the Takahe Mission - 'Monitoring the Southern Indo-Pacific from Space' - led by Restore Lab Ltd (NZ$2,838,000) with ASII (up to A$1.44m), developing SPACE-BASED RADAR SYSTEMS FOR MARITIME DOMAIN AWARENESS across the Australia-NZ region. A second project (University of Auckland with ANU, NZ$1.5m) creates coordinated optical ground stations for satellite laser communications. This is the most defence-relevant bilateral space activity identified, and it sits in the CIVIL science-funding channel.
label: FACT
source_title: Catalyst: Strategic - Australia New Zealand Collaborative Space Programme

name: New Zealand ground-based space infrastructure (GBSI) authorisation regime
scope: Outer Space and High-altitude Activities Amendment Act 2025 (2025 No 38), assent 25 July 2025, in force 29 July 2025. Brings all NZ ground infrastructure that communicates with, tracks, identifies or surveils a space object under a national-interest authorisation regime, with power under s49D(1)(b) to prohibit an authorisation holder from carrying out activities 'on behalf, or for the benefit, of a specified person or class of persons'. Regulations amended 7 May 2026; automatic authorisation for in-scope operators expires 29 July 2026.
notes: Not a partnership vehicle but a REGULATORY GATE recorded here because it governs any future Australian ground-segment activity in New Zealand - which is precisely the opportunity NZ's geography invites. Statute text downloaded and extracted locally. The transition deadline falls 8 days after this baseline's as-at date; authorisation status of NZ's SSA-relevant stations is a time-critical validation item.
label: FACT
